subject: Physics
description: Newton's law, escape velocity, satellites, weight vs mass

questions.stem: Newton's UNIVERSAL law of gravitation says the force between two masses is:

options.option_text: Inversely proportional to product of masses

questions.explanation: Newton's universal gravitation (1687, Principia): F = G(m₁m₂)/r². Force is DIRECTLY proportional to product of masses, INVERSELY proportional to SQUARE of distance. G = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² (Universal Gravitational Constant — measured by Cavendish, 1798, with torsion balance). For two 1-kg masses at 1 m: F = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N (very tiny). Inverse-square law also for: electric force (Coulomb), light intensity, sound intensity. Distractor 1 — confused direct/inverse. Distractor 3 — wrong dependence on r.

questions.stem: ESCAPE VELOCITY from Earth's surface is approximately:

options.option_text: Speed of light, the universal limit

questions.explanation: Escape velocity v_esc = √(2gR) = √(2 × 9.8 × 6.4 × 10⁶) ≈ 11.2 km/s = ~40,300 km/h. Speed needed to escape Earth's gravity without further propulsion (ignoring air drag). Beyond this, object follows hyperbolic trajectory. Moon escape velocity = 2.4 km/s; Sun = 618 km/s; Black hole = c (speed of light) at event horizon. Independent of object's mass. ORBITAL velocity at surface ≈ 7.9 km/s (less than escape; circular orbit). Rockets must reach escape velocity to leave Earth.

questions.stem: An astronaut feels WEIGHTLESS in orbit because:

options.option_text: Gravity is zero in space at orbit
He / she + the spacecraft are in free fall
Air pressure is zero in vacuum of space

questions.explanation: Common misconception — astronauts feel weightless NOT because there's no gravity (gravity is still ~89% of surface value at ISS altitude of 400 km). They are in CONTINUOUS FREE FALL toward Earth — but their horizontal velocity is so high they 'miss' the Earth, falling around it. Both spacecraft + astronaut accelerate at the same rate → no relative acceleration → feels like zero weight. Same effect: in a free-falling elevator, you'd feel weightless. Distractor 1 — wrong. Distractor 4 — partly true in rotating frame (centrifugal), but free-fall description is more fundamental.

questions.stem: GEOSTATIONARY SATELLITES (TV broadcasting) orbit at approximately:
questions.explanation: GEOSTATIONARY ORBIT — special orbit where satellite's period = Earth's rotation period (24 h sidereal ≈ 23h 56m 4s). Result: satellite appears STATIONARY over a point on equator. Altitude must be ~35,786 km (~36,000 km). Only over EQUATOR (latitude must be 0). Used for: TV/radio broadcasting (DirecTV, Tata Sky, dish antennas don't need to track), weather monitoring (INSAT, GSAT — Indian), some communications. ISRO's GSAT series, Cartosat, etc. INSAT-1 (1983) was India's first geostationary satellite. LOW EARTH ORBIT (LEO) ~200-2000 km — used by Hubble, ISS, OneWeb, Starlink.

questions.stem: WEIGHT differs from MASS in that:

options.option_text: Mass changes with location, weight is constant
Weight changes with location, mass is constant
Mass is measured in newtons (force unit)

questions.explanation: MASS = amount of matter (kg). Constant everywhere (unless extreme — Einstein's relativity). WEIGHT = gravitational force on mass (N): W = mg. Changes with location: surface of Earth (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²) → 60-kg person weighs ~588 N. Surface of Moon (g ≈ 1.62) → same person ~98 N (1/6th). In FREE FALL or orbit (effective g = 0) → weightless. Mass is INERTIAL property; weight is gravitational FORCE. Common usage 'I weigh 60 kg' really means 'mass 60 kg'.

questions.stem: If Earth were to SHRINK to half its present radius (without mass change), the value of g at its surface would:

options.option_text: Stay the same at 9.8 m/s² always

questions.explanation: g = GM/R². Mass M unchanged; radius R → R/2 means R² → R²/4. So g → 4g = 39.2 m/s². Inverse-square dependence on R. Conversely, if Earth's radius doubled (M same), g would become g/4. (If mass also changed proportionally to volume, the answer differs — but the question specifies mass unchanged.)

questions.stem: Kepler's THIRD LAW states that the square of the orbital period is proportional to:

options.option_text: Cube of the semi-major axis (T² ∝ a³)
Square of the semi-major axis (T² ∝ a²)
First power of orbit radius (T² ∝ a)
Mass of the orbiting body itself

questions.explanation: Kepler's 3 LAWS of planetary motion: 1st (Orbit Law) — planets move in ELLIPSES with Sun at one focus. 2nd (Area Law) — line from sun to planet sweeps equal areas in equal times (planet faster when closer). 3rd (Period Law) — T² ∝ a³ (where a = semi-major axis). For our solar system, Earth: T = 1 yr, a = 1 AU. Mars: T ≈ 1.88 yr, a ≈ 1.52 AU; check: 1.88² ≈ 3.53; 1.52³ ≈ 3.51 ✓. Newton derived Kepler's laws from gravitation. Distractor 4 — period independent of orbiting body's mass (Galileo's principle for free fall extended to gravity).
